meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'd like to know why my son's essay got a zero before anyone called me.
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. People draft elsewhere and paste it in. You haven't told me whether anyone asked Owen about this before the zero went in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Then whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
I'm searching the scene. A seventeen-year-old misquotes Shakespeare, Hale; that isn't a crime. Is it the only line?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Okay. I've written both down. What are you proposing for Owen?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called revising. You still haven't answered what you're proposing.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. Owen will do the rewrite, to put this behind him. I want it in writing tonight, nothing on his record, and the principal copied.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth is fine. Put the time and the room in the email, along with the new mark going in before December 1.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still want the time and room confirmed, the new mark entered before December 1, and an answer on whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero was entered. I expect all of it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants the time and room, the mark in before December 1, and an answer on whether Owen was heard first; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You turned the laptop to her and read out the version history with its times, because she could check it herself and it was dated.
What cost ground: You never answered whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in, so she kept coming back to it and kept her guard up.
What she never said: One night in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with a late-night creation and two big edits minutes apart the night before the due date, came close to that kind of night, but it proves nothing about the essay, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was spoken to before the zero went in, answer it in one plain sentence before showing any document.
